record.original_question: Are either of the Borel-cover properties S_1(B_Ω, B_Ω) or S_fin(B_Ω, B_Ω) hereditary, meaning that every subspace of a space with the property must also have the property?

evidence.quote: Problem 8.1 ([6, Problem 4], [31, Question 6]). Is any of the properties S1(BΩ, BΩ) or Sfin(BΩ, BΩ) hereditary?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X be an infinite topological space (in practice, a separable metrizable space such as a set of real numbers). A countable family U of Borel subsets of X is called a Borel ω-cover of X if X is not a member of U and every finite subset F of X is contained in some U in U. Denote by B_Ω = B_Ω(X) the collection of all countable Borel ω-covers of X.

For two families A and B of covers of X, define the selection principles:
• S_1(A, B): For every sequence (U_n : n ∈ ω) with each U_n ∈ A, one can choose U_n ∈ U_n for each n such that {U_n : n ∈ ω} ∈ B.
• S_fin(A, B): For every sequence (U_n : n ∈ ω) with each U_n ∈ A, one can choose finite subsets F_n ⊆ U_n such that the union ⋃_n F_n is a member of B.

A topological property P is said to be hereditary if every subspace of a space with property P also has property P.

Question: Is the property S_1(B_Ω, B_Ω) hereditary? Is the property S_fin(B_Ω, B_Ω) hereditary?
artifact.status_search_result: The hereditariness of S_1(B_Ω, B_Ω) and S_fin(B_Ω, B_Ω) is a known problem in the selection-principles literature on Borel covers, listed among open problems by Scheepers and Tsaban. Web searches surface related results (e.g., examples of subgroups of ℝ whose finite powers satisfy S_1(B_Ω, B_Ω), hereditariness for F_σ subsets of Scheepers-diagram properties), but no source clearly establishes a full positive or negative answer to either question. Current status is therefore not conclusively determinable from the available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Selection principles in mathematics: A milestone of open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Collected open problems concerning hereditariness of selection-principle classes including S_1(B_Ω, B_Ω) and S_fin(B_Ω, B_Ω).
status_evidence.claim: The hereditariness of these Borel-cover selection principles is listed as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: The combinatorics of Borel covers
status_evidence.snippet: Develops selection principles for Borel covers and equates several Borel-cover classes with their open-cover counterparts.
status_evidence.claim: Background paper introducing and studying B_Ω-type selection principles.

status_evidence.title: Selection principles in topology: New directions (Scheepers)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of selection-principle directions, including hereditariness questions for Borel-cover classes.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates that hereditariness questions for these classes are a guiding open theme.
